notes: Access: same as Bestsellers/Clearance files - tier 1 direct HTTP blocked by Cloudflare 429 challenge, tier 2 Playwright/CDP headless Chromium succeeded after warming up on the homepage; Claude-in-Chrome not needed. Discovery: grepped collections.json (372 collections) for new-arrival/new-in/just-in/latest/new-collection/whats-new terms, and checked main nav - the header has a first-class 'NEW' link (appears 3x in the desktop/mobile nav markup) pointing straight to /collections/new-arrivals, confirming this is the site's own primary New Arrivals concept. Opened it: rendered '27 Products', a real filterable/sortable PLP; INCLUDED. Two other 'new'-named collections were investigated and excluded: (1) /collections/new-home-collection, page title 'Freedom Tree NEST - Calm Home Collection' with 60 products - this is a themed/branded aesthetic sub-line ('NEST'), not a recency-based listing; nothing on the page frames it as newly-added stock, so it was excluded as a themed collection rather than flagged, per the brief's guidance that 'New Collection'-style names need inspection and marketing/themed pages are excluded. (2) /collections/new-on-sale ('New On Sale') - by its own name this is a newly-added-to-the-sale-rail collection, i.e. a Sale/markdown concept, not a New Arrivals concept; excluded. No genuine sub-structure (e.g. category-split New Arrivals) exists on the site - only the one flat /collections/new-arrivals listing.

rows.evidence: Rendered collection page text '27 Products'; linked from the main site header nav as 'NEW'; confirmed exhaustively via /collections/new-arrivals/products.json?limit=250 = 27 unique product IDs on a single page (<250, no further pages).
